examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/s3-consu.description: S3 event notifications: the CDK bucket's Lambda, SQS and SNS configurations delivered the documented s3:TestEvent on configuration; the two ObjectCreated configurations share the incoming/ prefix with non-overlapping suffixes, and a real SDK PUT of incoming/a.json delivered ObjectCreated:Put to the Lambda function only (which wrote a real SQS receipt) while the SNS .csv suffix and the queue's event type filtered it; a real SDK PUT of incoming/b.csv delivered ObjectCreated:Put to the SNS topic only; ignored/a.txt was filtered by every prefix/suffix rule; a real SDK DELETE delivered ObjectRemoved:Delete to the queue; describe reported exact per-destination delivered/filtered counts (lambda 1/3, queue 2/3, topic 2/3).

examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/rule-pub.gap: ElasticMQ emulates SQS and moto emulates SNS; the runner serves the EventBridge bus. IAM policy evaluation is a docs/125 true limit. The PutEvents calls, pattern matching, input shaping, target delivery, retries and DLQ are real.
examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/rule-pub.description: EventBridge rule targets: the publisher calls PutEvents through the real SDK for four rules on the default and a custom bus; the transformed event names that bus by ARN (the Fn::GetAtt form PutEvents documents) while the others use its name; an SQS target receives its InputPath body, an SNS target receives the input-transformer message, a Lambda target receives the static Input object, and a failing Lambda target exhausts two retries into the real DLQ with the documented error attributes.

examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/rule-tar.description: EventBridge Lambda rule target; it writes the received Input object to a real SQS receipt queue.

examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/rule-fai.description: EventBridge failing Lambda rule target; it always throws so the retry policy and DLQ are proven on the real path.

examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/worker.m.gap: ElasticMQ emulates SQS; IAM, KMS encryption and AWS-managed scaling are not emulated.
examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/worker.m.description: SQS worker handler: the EventsConsumer mapping batched two real ElasticMQ messages on the 10s window and left only the reported failure; FilteredConsumer deleted a non-matching message without invocation; FifoConsumer kept a failed group's records in order; ConcurrencyConsumer's live peak stayed at MaximumConcurrency=2.

examples/cdk/ssr-only-provided-assets-si.gap: CloudFront edge network (docs/125 true limit); the AWS_IAM Function URL is reached through local SigV4 OAC signing, but IAM policy evaluation is not emulated.
examples/cdk/ssr-only-provided-assets-si.description: SSR_ONLY provided assets: the real handler runs behind an AWS_IAM Function URL origin with local OAC signing and echoes the viewer request id; the provided bucket serves app.js, site.css and probe.txt; a missing object is 403 under OAC and OPTIONS is refused.

examples/cdk/ssr-site/bin/apptheory-ssr-.gap: CloudFront edge network (docs/125 true limit); the gateway forwards a streamed response at the origin's pace and caches it in full after it completes (Lambda's 6 MB uncapped burst and 2 MBps streaming cap are not reproduced).
examples/cdk/ssr-site/bin/apptheory-ssr-.description: SSR site: the origin group fails over from the S3 HTML primary (403 under OAC) to the real SSR handler; the SSR stream reaches the viewer through the gateway and directly on the Function URL as the handler writes it, the viewer-response function echoes the request id, and the assets and hydrate deployments, full and ranged HEAD, conditional If-None-Match GETs, OPTIONS and the missing-object 403 are asserted. Caching is real: the static-assets behavior answered a miss then a hit with x-cache and age, the CACHING_DISABLED SSR behavior never cached, an invalidation through the local API and through the aws CLI removed the object, and clock.advance past the TTL was a miss again.

examples/cdk/ssr-site/scripts/generate-a.gap: CloudFront edge network (docs/125 true limit); the manifest is matched against the gateway response, not a deployed bucket.
examples/cdk/ssr-site/scripts/generate-a.description: SSR site asset manifest generator: runs against the real assets directory, asserts hello.txt's sha256 and byte count, then matches the served asset through the gateway to the manifest.

examples/cdk/ssr-site/scripts/upload-ass.gap: The edge network and IAM policy evaluation are docs/125 true limits (real network properties; IAM policy evaluation in general).
examples/cdk/ssr-site/scripts/upload-ass.description: SSR site asset uploader: the real AWS CLI syncs the assets and copies the generated manifest to the local s3proxy endpoint with dummy credentials; the gateway serves both with the script's cache-control and the uploaded manifest. The site's bucket declares no event notification; the notification destinations are proven by the sqs-queue row. s3proxy serves the objects without bucket policies or IAM.

examples/cdk/codebuild-job-runner/bin/ap.description: CodeBuild job runner CDK app, synthesized and hash-checked with focused project, state-change-rule and grant assertions.

examples/cdk/edge-gateway/bin/app.ts.gap: CloudFront edge network and edge TLS (docs/125 true limits); viewer events run against the viewer's plain-HTTP connection, so ViewerProtocolPolicy is reported rather than enforced. The field-level encryption row needs the AWS Encryption SDK on the harness interpreter.
examples/cdk/edge-gateway/bin/app.ts.description: Edge gateway: four Lambda@Edge associations run through the real Node containers (viewer-request uri rewrite, origin-request generated response cached without a second invocation, origin-response body replacement, viewer-response header), IncludeBody exposes the base64 body, an origin rewrite reaches the other declared origin, a runtime 2.0 CloudFront Function reads get/exists/meta from its key value store, geo restriction serves US, refuses JP and serves an undetermined location, and the origin decrypts the field-level encryption ciphertext with the real AWS Encryption SDK.

examples/cdk/edge-gateway/handlers/viewe.description: Lambda@Edge viewer-request handler: uri and query rewrite, a header returned without a key, an IncludeBody body header and a generated response.

examples/cdk/edge-gateway/handlers/origi.description: Lambda@Edge origin-request handler: a generated response with an invocation counter and an origin rewrite.
Lambda@Edge origin-response handler: a header and a body replacement.

examples/cdk/edge-gateway/handlers/viewe.description: Lambda@Edge viewer-response handler: a header on responses that may run it.

examples/cdk/edge-gateway/handlers/kvs.j.description: CloudFront Function runtime 2.0 handler: get (string and json formats), exists and meta against the associated key value store.

scripts/local/runtime_api_conformance.py.description: Runtime API conformance: one handler set per language on the real digest-pinned runtime images, run once under the embedded Runtime Interface Emulator and once under the runner's Lambda Runtime API, comparing status, headers, body bytes, handler errors, timeouts and initialization failures.
scripts/local/runtime_api_conformance.py.gap: The comparison runs this host's architecture; the Lambda service's Init-phase billing and its 10-second Init limit are not emulated.
